A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same NOVA study. The main text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–H are available and can be matched despite pagination and layout changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original NOVA image/video benchmark results, architectural ablations, and appendix experiments on extrapolation and inference time.

after.justification: v2 retains these original NOVA results, including Tables 2–6 and the extrapolation and architectural analyses.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Appendices A–B retain temporal frame-by-frame prediction, spatial set-by-set prediction, BOV-based scaling and shifting, normalization, and the per-token diffusion objective. No proposed procedure or component changes.

E1.justification: The training data sources and T2I-CompBench, GenEval, DPG-Bench, and VBench evaluations remain unchanged. Image-conditioned generation, multiple conditioning contexts, and video extrapolation scenarios are also retained.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in Tables 2, 3, and 6 and Figure 4. Some baseline names disappear from the shortened discussion but remain in the comparisons. The newly cited Loong work is not evaluated.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 retains the model sizes, training settings, guidance of 7.0, 128 autoregressive steps, and five video samples per prompt. Appendix C retains the 200-video PSNR/LPIPS evaluation. Omitted ablation documentation does not establish a changed experimental procedure.

E4.justification: The temporal-modeling, decomposition-rank, and normalization ablations remain in Figures 8–10. Appendices C–E retain the extrapolation, inference-time, and quantitative TAM analyses; no analysis or supporting example is added or removed.

E5.justification: Sampling and statistical reporting remain unchanged. Neither version introduces independent-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Numerical tables, plotted curves, and generated examples are unchanged. However, Section 4.3 removes specific qualitative findings, notably the observation that adding text produces more natural perspective movements. This reduces reported observations without establishing a performance change.

T1.justification: The probability factorizations, definitions, diffusion loss, and denoising equations in Section 3 are unchanged. No formal assumptions, theorems, or proofs are added or removed.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims concerning non-quantized autoregressive generation, efficiency, visual quality, and contextual generalization.

C2.justification: v2 removes the inference that plausible motion demonstrates understanding of fundamental physics, including interaction forces and fluid dynamics. It also removes the blanket statement about causal modeling's superiority over multitask approaches. The extrapolation and text-rendering limitations in Appendices C and F remain.

D1.justification: v2 omits Section 4.4's explicit description of replacing temporal attention with bidirectional attention and predicting random token sets across the entire video for the TAM ablation. Appendix E retains discussion of bidirectional attention but not the full procedure. Other implementation and code/model access disclosures remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2.2 and the bibliography add Loong: Generating Minute-Level Long Videos with Autoregressive Language Models, cited as Wang et al. (2024b). The broader positioning relative to MAR, Emu3, and diffusion models is unchanged.

P1.justification: Sections 4.2–4.4 undergo localized condensation. Affiliations, corresponding-author information, and acknowledgements are expanded, and the conference header is added. The main section sequence and appendix organization remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 9's raster plots are replaced with vector rendering while retaining their curves, axes, and legends. Figures and surrounding prose are repositioned, including moving Figure 10 onto the preceding page. Tables and figure content otherwise remain intact.

improvement.justification: Removing the inference about fundamental physics makes the interpretation more cautious, and Figure 9 becomes clearer. However, v2 also loses the explicit TAM-ablation procedure, reducing reproducibility detail. With the empirical evidence unchanged, these limited benefits and harms do not establish a reliable net quality direction.
